findings.title: Working-hours check rejects any slot that falls outside any single working-hours range
findings.body: The working-hours guard uses `workingHours.find(...)` and returns false if the callback is truthy. The callback is truthy whenever one particular range does not contain the slot. So for a day with several ranges (for example 9-12 and 14-18, or aggregated hours from multiple hosts), a slot inside one range is rejected because it is outside another. The intended semantics is 'outside all ranges', which needs `every`/`some` logic. Also `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of the slot end, so `end > workingHour.endTime` checks the start, not the end. Finally, the comparison uses UTC day and hour while `WorkingHours` values are minutes in the organizer timezone (per the type doc), so the check is evaluated in the wrong timezone. This is a regression that can remove valid slots for any multi-range or cross-timezone schedule.

findings.title: Comparing dayjs objects with === is always false
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares object identity, not time. The branch that treats a zero-length override as a special case never runs. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `valueOf()`.

findings.title: Date override logic accepts partially overlapping slots and rejects slots when several overrides share a day
findings.body: `dateOverrideExist` is set true for any override on the same day, and `find` returns true (meaning 'reject') as soon as any override on that day does not contain the slot. Consequences: (1) with two overrides on the same day, a slot inside override A is rejected because it is outside override B. (2) A slot that starts before an override's start and ends after it (partial overlap) matches none of the rejection conditions. It falls through to `return true` and is accepted even though it is not fully inside the override. The containment test must be: slot start >= override start and slot end <= override end, evaluated across all overrides for the day, with a clear rule for when no override covers the slot.

findings.title: Organizer timezone offset sign looks inverted for override conversion
findings.body: `utcOffset = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` negates the organizer's offset. For Asia/Kolkata (+330) this shifts the override by -330 minutes, so the local day of the override is computed incorrectly. The same override is then compared against `slotStartTime.format(...)` in UTC, which mixes frames. The PR's timezone fix depends on this conversion, so it needs verification with a concrete example (an override near midnight in the organizer zone).

findings.title: Override timezone conversion depends on an optional field that may be undefined
findings.body: `override.timeZone` is typed optional in the flattened override (it is set from `availability.timeZone`, which `getUserAvailability` may leave undefined). `dayjs(...).tz(undefined)` then falls back to the local runtime timezone, which differs between server and browser. The computed offset becomes environment dependent. The code should either require the timezone or fall back explicitly to the organizer timezone that `getSlots` already receives. Also, `startTime`/`endTime` are computed as minutes of day only, so an override spanning midnight after the offset shift produces endTime < startTime and is silently dropped by the boundary logic.

findings.title: New timezone test does not exercise the bug it claims to cover
findings.body: The added test asserts that the same UTC slots are returned for the attendee timezone +6:00 as for +5:30. It reuses the existing expectation, so it passes whether or not overrides are adjusted correctly. It does not cover the reported case: an organizer override whose organizer timezone differs from the schedule timezone, where the attendee's timezone should change which slots appear. No test covers the round-robin fixed-host override fix either, which is the primary change in the description.
